on_screen: Title card: Melinting dance · Indonesia · 16th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in the 16th century under Ratu Melinting II.
It was originally called Cetik Kipas and was exclusively performed by the royal family.
In 1965, President Sukarno renamed it Melinting and introduced it to a national audience at Istora Senayan.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed at traditional events to welcome guests and express gratitude for happiness.
It also illustrates the majesty of Ratu Melinting.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
on_screen: Formation: Divided into four rounds: opening, kugowo queen, floating kenui, and closing.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music features the Kalo Bala, kendang, gongs, gamelan, and fiddle.
It is used to accompany dancers into the arena and signal respect for guests.
Listen for the Kalo Bala, kendang, gongs, gamelan.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Men wear tapis cloth, belanga shirts, seretei feathers, fans, and gold skullcaps.
Women wear tapis pepadun, white kebaya, yellow veils, jukum fruit, and ruwi bracelets.
Make-up is essential for setting the atmosphere.
